description: Structured clustering & seeding rules consumed by the sf-srs drafting flow (`srs-cli.sh draft --from codebase`). SKILL.md points to this file; edit here, not in prose.
reading_findings: Every shape has `kind` + `title` — use them for first-pass clustering.
`area` is the glue: findings that share an `area` usually belong to the same Epic / FR cluster.
`file` is the authoritative path — quote it back to the user when proposing a cluster.
`endpoint.hasTests` flags `true` when the same `area` has at least one test finding — use it to prime the TC section.
`ui-flow.linkedEndpointGuess` is a soft hint (filename / route substring match) — verify before trusting.
`doc-context.excerpt` is capped at 280 chars — treat it as a summary seed, not the full text.

steps.name: Group by area
steps.action: Collect every finding whose `area` matches. Add `doc-context` findings that share the area name or a parent folder.

steps.name: Pick the Epic level
steps.action: One Epic per coherent area (e.g. `auth`, `storage`, `accounts`). Title + narrative come from the richest `doc-context` in the group, or from the user's wording.

steps.name: Propose the FRs
rules: One FR per `endpoint` (or per tight endpoint cluster — CRUD on the same resource collapses into one FR).
Reuse `ui-flow` routes as acceptance criteria on the user-facing FR.
Populate `dsRefs` / `tcRefs` from the items seeded in step 4 so the FR surfaces traceability links.

steps.name: Seed the Epic-level DS / TC / NFR sections
steps.action: Every Epic carries the SRS five-category shape (UR + FR + DS + TC + NFR). See `templates/examples/example-epic.md` (rendered) and `templates/examples/example-epic.spec.json` (machine-readable) for the exact layout. Apply the `seeding` rules below.

steps.name: Flag gaps
steps.action: Any `endpoint` with `hasTests=false` is a test-coverage gap — surface it as a **TODO** TC item (title `"{METHOD} {PATH} — happy path"`, `expectedResult: "to write"`), not silently.

seeding.philosophy: Scanners surface raw material, the agent synthesises items. Reuse the L1+L2+L3 pattern from the eval: deterministic findings feed AI prompts, the agent always runs, the user always validates before write.

ds_items.description: One `DsItem` per material design decision visible in code.

mappings.finding: endpoint with non-trivial DTO (POST/PATCH body ≥ 2 fields)
mappings.title: API contract — <METHOD> <path>
mappings.description_source: DTO field list + validation rules surfaced by class-validator decorators

mappings.title: UI form — <PageName>
mappings.description_source: form field list + linkedEndpointGuess if present

grouping_rules: Set `frRefs` to every FR in the group whose endpoint/entity/UI flow matches.
Deduplicate by title prefix — if two entities share the same core name (e.g. `User` + `UserProfile`), collapse into a single DS item with both sub-models listed in the description.

mappings.rule: parse Given/When/Then from the title if phrased that way, else bullet the `describe` chain

mappings.source: assertion in the test body (if readable)

todo_for_untested_endpoints.emit_as: TODO TC item (the drift is auditable, not invisible)
reviewer_options: accept the TODO (making the gap part of the public contract)

nfr_items.description: NFRs are **proposed, not derived** — every seeded item must be marked for explicit human validation. Always emit with `priority: 'P3'` and `target: '<proposed — needs human validation>'`. The reviewer lifts priority / refines target before accepting.

layer1_stack_signals.signal: auth module present (endpoints under /auth/* or Prisma Session / RefreshToken model)
seeded_nfrs: Security — JWT access token expiry ≤ 15 min
Security — refresh token rotation on every use
Security — login rate limit ≤ 5 attempts / minute / IP

layer1_stack_signals.signal: i18n module (src/locales/ folder or i18next dep)
seeded_nfrs: i18n — all user-facing strings translated in FR + EN
a11y — locale switchable without page reload
Data — soft delete via deletedAt on user-owned entities
Ops — API health check p95 ≤ 1 s

layer1_stack_signals.signal: Playwright or e2e spec files present
seeded_nfrs: Quality — e2e coverage on critical user flows (login, signup, checkout when applicable)
Docs — OpenAPI spec regenerated on every API change (CI guard)

layer2_standard_saas_catalogue.nfr: Perf — p95 API latency ≤ 500 ms at 100 req/s sustained
Security — all user-uploaded files virus-scanned before persistence
Privacy — PII fields encrypted at rest
layer2_standard_saas_catalogue.condition: only if schema carries email, phone, address

coverage_table.purpose: Before firing the review prompt on an Epic cluster, emit a one-shot coverage table so the reviewer sees what got seeded per category and where it came from.
template: │ TC   │ 8 (+ 2 TODO)  │ test.cases[] across 3 spec files             │
│ NFR  │ 4 (proposed)  │ auth + i18n + prisma + playwright signals    │
coverage_table.red_flag: A cluster with **zero DS or zero TC** is a red flag — either the area is genuinely pure UI glue (no data model, no tests yet) or the scanners missed something. Surface the anomaly in the review prompt rather than silently proposing an Epic with empty sections.

review_loop.rule: Never write to Notion without confirmation. Drive the loop one cluster at a time.
prompt_template: 🔍 J'ai trouvé <N> éléments dans le scanner pour le domaine `<area>`. Je te propose de créer :
└─ gaps : <endpoint without tests>, <page without linked endpoint>
Je pars sur cette structure, ou tu veux retailler l'Epic ? [accept / edit / reject / skip-area]

branches.accept: serialise the cluster as DraftCandidate[] and call `srs-cli.sh write --spec <tmp.json>`
branches.edit: negotiate the title / narrative / FR split and re-confirm
branches.skip-area: park the area and continue with the next

review_loop.throttle: Never batch-accept more than one Epic per prompt — the reviewer has to be able to course-correct cluster by cluster.
